domain: international trademark examination / designation-level refusal outcome prediction (WIPO Madrid System)
prediction_question: The lead probed was the WIPO Madrid System's international trademark registry: a new international registration (or subsequent designation) designates one or more Madrid members, and each designated office examines the mark and may issue a notification of provisional refusal within its treaty time limit, or a statement of grant of protection. The natural task was designation-level: at the Gazette publication of a new international registration, for designation (registration, member M) with notification date T, predict whether the office of M will publish a notification of provisional refusal (total or partial) within the applicable 12/18-month window from T. The task shape was attractive: a treaty-documented censoring window (Article 5(2) Agreement / 5(2)(a)-(c) Protocol; Rule 16 'possible opposition beyond the 18-month time limit' entries exist as a separate Gazette chapter), a weekly official publication carrying both the new registrations and the outcome events (refusal, confirmation, grant), large volume (~60k+ international registrations per year in recent years, each with several designations), and no known ML-ready precedent. The session closed the lead on licence grounds before any row-level probing: every free machine-readable channel for this registry carries service-specific terms that prohibit exactly what a published derived dataset is.
prediction_time: Would have been the Thursday publication of the international registration in the WIPO Gazette of International Marks (weekly, official publication), with the prediction made at that publication instant using the published registration attributes (mark, Nice classes, holder, office of origin, designated members and their notification dates) - never reached: licence triage (first, cheapest) vetoed the source before schema, volume or split probing, per the standing order of work.
target_definition: Would have been binary: at least one Gazette 'Notifications of provisional refusals' entry (or 'Confirmations of total provisional refusal (Rule 18ter(3))') for (registration, member M) inside the window vs no such entry, with the no-refusal negative class bounded by the treaty window (a documented censoring boundary, which is what made the lead worth probing) - never reached. The label source would have been the refusal/grant chapters of the Gazette and the Madrid Monitor designation-status history; recorded here only so the shape of the closed lead is documented; the verdict is a licence rejection, not a task finding.

sources.name: WIPO Madrid Monitor database (www3.wipo.int/madrid/monitor/en/), the search service over international applications and registrations under the Madrid System
sources.api: No public API: 'I want to integrate your database into my project, do you have a public API for direct search access? Not currently.' (Madrid Monitor help/FAQ page, read 2026-10-31 via live-page extraction); the complete Madrid backfile 'is available for a fee' (same page). Download options are per-page-of-results only (PDF/CSV/XLSX/HTML/XML of the visible page; ZIP of the page's XML source files).
sources.license: Madrid Monitor Database Terms of Use (July 2025), https://www3.wipo.int/madrid/monitor/en/terms.jsp - class D clauses quoted in license_evidence.

sources.name: WIPO Gazette of International Marks (official weekly publication of the Madrid System)
sources.api: Browse-by-chapter search UI over weekly issues (2026-10-31 measured: issues 42 - 29/10/2026 back to 01 - 15/01/2026 for 2026; year selector 2009-2026 plus 'All'; a 1997-2010 PDF archive at https://www.wipo.int/madrid/en/madridgazette/year.html). Chapters measured on the page include: Registrations; Subsequent designations; Notifications of provisional refusals; Final decisions; Confirmations of total provisional refusal (Rule 18ter(3)); Statements of grant of protection following a provisional refusal (Rule 18ter(2)); Statements of grant of protection (Rule 18ter(1)); Possible opposition beyond the 18-month time limit (Rule 16); Invalidations. The Gazette is served INSIDE the Madrid Monitor web application (path /madrid/monitor/en/), whose Terms of Use govern the same application.
sources.license: Same Madrid Monitor service terms (the Gazette is a view of the Madrid Monitor database within that application); the WIPO website-general open-access policy applies only 'unless service-specific terms of use apply' (https://www.wipo.int/en/web/terms-of-use).

license_evidence: Madrid Monitor Database: Terms of Use (July 2025), https://www3.wipo.int/madrid/monitor/en/terms.jsp, fetched 2026-10-31 - section 4: '(b) Unless otherwise provided for in these Terms of Use, the User shall have a worldwide, limited, revocable, non-transferable and non-exclusive right to use data contained in the Madrid Monitor database as follows: (i) query the data in the Madrid Monitor database; (ii) view, download and store individual documents. (c) Any use other than those specifically authorized above shall require the prior written consent of WIPO.'

Same instrument, section 5 (Prohibited Use): '(a) The User does not have the right to make the following uses of data contained in the Madrid Monitor database: (i) perform bulk acquisition, bulk downloads or bulk storing of data or documents; (ii) perform bulk copying, bulk reformatting or bulk redistribution of data or documents'.

Same instrument, section 6 (Fair Use Policy): the service 'is not designed for bulk downloads'; the User shall not undertake 'more than 10 search related actions per minute from an IP address; and (ii) automated queries'; and '(c) Under no circumstances may the information made available through the Madrid Monitor database be made accessible or sublicensed in any way to another service provider host or publisher.' - a GitHub/Hugging Face release of derived rows is exactly the prohibited bulk reformatting plus sublicensing to another publisher.

Global Brand Database (the other free channel that includes Madrid records) Terms of Use (November 2022), https://www.wipo.int/en/web/global-brand-database/terms_and_conditions, fetched 2026-10-31 - section 2.1: 'the User is forbidden to: ... 2. perform automated queries; 3. perform bulk acquisition, bulk downloading, and bulk storing of data; 4. perform bulk copying, bulk reformatting, bulk sharing and bulk redistributing of data; 5. perform web scraping'; section 2.2: 'Under no circumstances may the data made available through Global Brand Database be sold or sublicensed by the User in any way without WIPO's permission.'; section 3.2: 'In addition to the Global Brand Database, WIPO may also provide the entire collection of all international marks recorded under the Madrid system on request and payment of a fee.' - i.e. the bulk Madrid data channel is a paid service, and the free channels forbid bulk and automated access.

WIPO general Terms of Use (https://www.wipo.int/en/web/terms-of-use, read 2026-10-31 via live-page extraction): 'Unless service-specific terms of use apply ...' - the site-wide CC BY 4.0 open-access policy is explicitly conditional, and the Madrid Monitor service terms above are exactly such service-specific terms, so they govern.
split_strategy: Not reached - licence class D stops the order of work at step 1 (licence and terms), before aggregates, schema or split probing. No volume, base rate, split capacity or cost was measured, by design. (Only the publication structure was read: the Gazette chapter list that would have carried the label events, and the Monitor's per-page download limits.)

measurements.licence_triage_2026_10_31: Madrid Monitor Terms of Use (terms.jsp) HTTP 200, full text read; Madrid Monitor help/FAQ (via live-page extraction): no public API ('Not currently'), complete backfile 'available for a fee', per-page download limits only, >10 searches/min and automated queries disallowed; Gazette portal (gazette.jsp) HTTP 200: weekly issues listed (No. 42 - 29/10/2026 back to No. 01 - 15/01/2026 for 2026; years 2009-2026 + All; 1997-2010 archive at wipo.int/madrid/en/madridgazette/year.html), chapters enumerated incl. 'Notifications of provisional refusals', 'Confirmations of total provisional refusal (Rule 18ter(3))', 'Statements of grant of protection (Rule 18ter(1))', 'Possible opposition beyond the 18-month time limit (Rule 16)', 'Invalidations'; GBD Terms of Use HTTP 200, sections 2.1-3.2 quoted in license_evidence. WIPO general ToU: CC BY 4.0 default explicitly conditional on absence of service-specific terms.
measurements.task_probes_deliberately_not_run: Under the standing licence-first order of work, no schema, volume, base-rate, split or cost probing was spent on this source after the class D instrument was read. The cost of this rejection was five page fetches plus one search sweep. Relevance note: the uncommitted ipo-trademark-registration-outcome work (UK IPO, a parallel session's output) shows the operator already has a national trademark-examination task in flight; this lead would have been the multi-member sibling.

rejection_reason: Licence class D on every free machine-readable channel. The publisher's own instrument for the registry data (Madrid Monitor Terms of Use, July 2025, which also hosts the Gazette) grants only query/view/store-individual-documents rights, states that any other use 'shall require the prior written consent of WIPO', explicitly prohibits bulk acquisition, bulk copying, bulk reformatting and bulk redistribution, prohibits automated queries and >10 search actions/minute, and states the information may 'under no circumstances' be made accessible or sublicensed to another service provider host or publisher. The Global Brand Database terms repeat the bulk/automated prohibitions verbatim and add a web-scraping prohibition. The complete backfile is a paid service. The site-wide WIPO CC BY 4.0 open-access policy does not lift this: it applies only where no service-specific terms exist, and here they do. A published dataset of derived Madrid designation/refusal rows is exactly the prohibited use, so this is closed under the standing policy (we build only on sources already clean), not parked.
next_action: None - closed on licence grounds. Re-open only if (a) WIPO attaches an explicit dataset-level open licence (e.g. CC BY) to a Madrid registry data channel - the general website policy does not count; or (b) the operator records a candidate-specific risk acceptance for this source, which would resolve licence ambiguity as a risk acceptance (never a grant) and would still leave the access problem (no public API, automated queries prohibited, backfile paid) needing a licensed channel; or (c) a national IP office publishes its own Madrid-refusal examination outcomes under its own open licence, which would be a different, single-jurisdiction candidate. The 1997-2010 Gazette archive sits on the main wipo.org domain, but current-years data - needed for any eval/holdout window - is served only through the Madrid Monitor application with its terms, so the archive cannot carry the task alone.

jurisdiction.publisher: World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO), headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland
jurisdiction.convention: The publisher's HQ country is recorded because 'international' is not a country. WIPO's own Terms of Use define it as 'an intergovernmental organization and specialized agency of the United Nations, which administers the Madrid System'; seat Geneva, Switzerland. This candidate is in this session's assigned region (international organisations) and its jurisdiction is non-US.

licence_note: Class D on the publisher's own instrument: Madrid Monitor Database Terms of Use (July 2025), the service-specific terms governing both the search service and the Gazette view; bulk acquisition/copying/reformatting/redistribution and automated queries are explicitly prohibited and any other use requires prior written consent; the GBD channel repeats the prohibitions and offers the full Madrid collection only as a paid service. The general WIPO CC BY 4.0 policy is conditional on the absence of service-specific terms and therefore does not apply.
